questions.questionText:
On 31 December 2025, T. Nyoni's Cash Book (bank column) showed a debit balance of $2,450, whereas the Bank Statement showed $2,890.
The following differences were found:
(i) Bank charges of $45 appeared on the Bank Statement only.
(ii) A credit transfer of $310 from debtor R. Dube was received directly by the bank.
(iii) Unpresented cheques totalled $640.
(iv) Cash banked on 31 December of $465 had not yet been credited by the bank.
Prepare (a) an Updated Cash Book [4 marks] and (b) a Bank Reconciliation Statement as at 31 December 2025 [4 marks].
questions.explanation:
(a) Updated Cash Book: Start Dr $2,450 + Credit transfer $310 - Bank charges $45 = Updated Dr Cash Book balance $2,715 [4 marks].
(b) Bank Reconciliation Statement:
Updated Cash Book Dr balance: $2,715
Add unpresented cheques: +$640 -> $3,355
Less uncredited lodgement: -$465
= Balance per Bank Statement: $2,890 [4 marks].

questions.questionText:
Enter the following Trial Balance adjustments for M. Chigumba for the year ended 31 December 2025 and show the exact Income Statement & Balance Sheet extracts:
- Trial balance Electricity expense: $1,800; Electricity owing at 31 Dec: $240.
- Trial balance Insurance expense: $960 (covers 12 months ending 31 March 2026).
- Delivery van cost $16,000, accumulated depreciation $3,200; depreciate at 20% reducing balance. [6 marks]
questions.explanation:
1. Electricity expense = $1,800 + $240 accrued = $2,040 (Income Statement); Current Liability Accrual = $240 [2 marks].
2. Insurance prepaid for 3 months (Jan–Mar 2026) = (3/12) × $960 = $240 (Current Asset). Insurance expense = $960 - $240 = $720 [2 marks].
3. Depreciation = 20% × ($16,000 - $3,200) = 20% × $12,800 = $2,560 expense; NBV on SOFP = $12,800 - $2,560 = $10,240 [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
From the following details of Chipo Traders, prepare the Trading and Profit & Loss Account (Income Statement) for the year ended 31 December 2025:
Sales $94,000; Sales Returns $2,000; Opening Inventory $8,500; Purchases $56,000; Carriage Inwards $1,500; Closing Inventory $10,000; Rent & Rates $7,200; Wages $11,800; Discount Received $900; General Expenses $3,400. [8 marks]

Prepare a Sales Ledger Control Account for August 2025 from these totals:
1 Aug Debtors balance $4,200; Credit sales $18,600; Cash received from debtors $16,400; Sales returns $520; Discount allowed $380; Bad debts written off $250; Dishonoured customer cheque $300. Find the closing Trade Receivables balance at 31 August. [6 marks]
questions.explanation:
Debit entries: Opening Bal $4,200 + Credit Sales $18,600 + Dishonoured Cheque $300 = $23,100 [3 marks].
Credit entries: Cash Received $16,400 + Sales Returns $520 + Discount Allowed $380 + Bad Debts $250 = $17,550 [2 marks].
Closing Balance c/d (Dr) = $23,100 - $17,550 = $5,550 [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
Show journal entries (with brief narratives) to correct the following errors after a Trial Balance had a Suspense credit balance of $540:
(a) Credit sales of $800 to P. Gumbo were completely omitted from the books.
(b) Repairs to office computer of $270 were debited in error to the Office Equipment account.
(c) The Purchases Day Book was overcast (added up too high) by $540. [6 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Error of Omission: Dr P. Gumbo $800, Cr Sales $800 (Record omitted credit sale) [2 marks].
(b) Error of Principle: Dr Computer Repairs $270, Cr Office Equipment $270 (Correct capital/revenue misclassification) [2 marks].
(c) Single-sided cast error: Dr Suspense $540, Cr Purchases $540 (Eliminates suspense credit balance) [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Kudzai and Farai are in partnership sharing profits and losses 3 : 2. Net Profit before appropriation is $42,000. Capital balances: Kudzai $40,000, Farai $30,000. Interest on capital is 10% p.a. Farai receives an annual partnership salary of $8,000. Interest on drawings: Kudzai $600, Farai $400.
Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account for the year. [7 marks]
questions.explanation:
Net Profit $42,000 + Interest on Drawings ($600 + $400 = $1,000) = $43,000 [2 marks].
Less Interest on Capital: Kudzai $4,000 + Farai $3,000 = $7,000 [2 marks].
Less Farai Salary: $8,000 -> Residual profit = $43,000 - $15,000 = $28,000 [1 mark].
Profit Share (3:2): Kudzai (3/5) = $16,800; Farai (2/5) = $11,200 [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A manufacturing firm reports for the year:
Opening raw materials $6,000; Raw material purchases $38,000; Closing raw materials $7,500; Direct factory wages $24,000; Factory power & rent $9,500; Depreciation of factory plant $4,000; Opening Work-in-Progress $3,200; Closing Work-in-Progress $2,700.
Calculate (a) Cost of Raw Materials Consumed, (b) Prime Cost, and (c) Total Production Cost of finished goods. [6 marks]

Mbare Sports Club had 120 members each paying $50 annual subscription. On 1 Jan 2025, 4 members owed subscriptions for 2024 and 6 members had paid for 2025 in advance. During 2025, cash received for subscriptions totalled $5,900. On 31 Dec 2025, 5 members had prepaid for 2026.
Prepare the Subscriptions Account showing the income transferred to Income & Expenditure Account and closing arrears. [6 marks]
questions.explanation:
Opening Arrears Dr = 4×50 = $200; Opening Advance Cr = 6×50 = $300 [1].
Cash received Cr = $5,900 [1].
Subscription Income for 120 members = 120 × 50 = $6,000 (transfer to I&E Dr) [2].
Closing Advance c/d (Dr side bal -> Cr b/d) = 5×50 = $250 [1].
Dr Total = 200 + 6,000 + 250 = $6,450; Cr Total so far = 300 + 5,900 = $6,200 -> Closing Arrears c/d = $250 (5 members owing) [1].

questions.questionText:
Given for Zvikomborero Enterprises:
Sales $120,000; Cost of Goods Sold $78,000; Operating Expenses $24,000; Opening Inventory $11,000; Closing Inventory $15,000; Capital Employed $90,000.
Calculate:
(a) Gross Profit Margin (%) [2 marks]
(b) Net Profit Margin (%) [2 marks]
(c) Rate of Inventory Turnover (times) [2 marks]
(d) Return on Capital Employed (ROCE %) [2 marks]

A machine was bought on 1 Jan 2023 for $18,000 cash. Depreciation is charged at 25% per annum straight-line with nil residual value. On 30 June 2025, the machine was sold for $7,200 by cheque (assume full year depreciation in year of purchase, none in year of sale).
Prepare the Machine Disposal Account showing profit or loss on sale. [5 marks]
questions.explanation:
2023 dep = $4,500; 2024 dep = $4,500 -> Accumulated Depreciation = $9,000 [2 marks].
Disposal Account: Dr Cost $18,000; Cr Provision for Depreciation $9,000; Cr Bank proceeds $7,200 [2 marks].
Net Book Value = $9,000 vs Proceeds $7,200 -> Loss on Disposal = $1,800 (Cr Income Statement) [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A trader did not keep full double-entry records. At 1 Jan 2025: Cash $1,200, Equipment $8,000, Inventory $4,500, Trade Receivables $2,800, Trade Payables $2,500. During the year she drew $3,600 for personal use and banked $2,000 extra capital. At 31 Dec 2025: Cash $1,900, Equipment $7,200, Inventory $5,200, Trade Receivables $3,400, Trade Payables $2,100.
Calculate (a) Opening Capital, (b) Closing Capital, and (c) Net Profit for 2025. [6 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Opening Assets = 1,200 + 8,000 + 4,500 + 2,800 = $16,500. Opening Capital = 16,500 - 2,500 = $14,000 [2 marks].
(b) Closing Assets = 1,900 + 7,200 + 5,200 + 3,400 = $17,700. Closing Capital = 17,700 - 2,100 = $15,600 [2 marks].
(c) Net Profit = Closing Cap - Opening Cap + Drawings - Capital Introduced = 15,600 - 14,000 + 3,600 - 2,000 = $3,200 [2 marks].

questions.questionText: State the difference between Bad Debts and Provision for Doubtful Debts, and show the Ledger entries when a customer owes $900, $400 is written off as irrecoverable, and a 5% provision is created on the remaining receivables balance of $10,000. [5 marks]
questions.explanation:
Bad debts are confirmed uncollectible debts written off immediately as an expense; a provision for doubtful debts is an estimated allowance against future expected defaults [2 marks].
Entries: Dr Bad Debts $400, Cr Debtor $400 (transfer $400 to Income Statement) [1.5]. New Provision = 5% × $10,000 = $500 (Dr Income Statement $500, Cr Provision for Doubtful Debts $500) [1.5].

questions.questionText: List six steps in the accounting cycle in logical chronological order from source documents to final financial statements. [6 marks]
questions.explanation: 1. Collect & verify source documents (invoices, receipts, credit notes). 2. Record in books of prime entry (journals/cash book). 3. Post to double-entry ledger accounts. 4. Balance ledger accounts & extract Trial Balance. 5. Make year-end adjustments (accruals, depreciation, provisions). 6. Prepare Income Statement & Statement of Financial Position [6 marks].

questions.questionText: Distinguish between a Two-Column Cash Book and a Three-Column Cash Book, and explain why the Discount columns are NOT part of double-entry cash balances. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: A two-column cash book has Cash and Bank columns on both sides; a three-column cash book adds Discount Allowed (Dr) and Discount Received (Cr) memorandum columns [2 marks]. Discount columns record totals transferred to Discount Allowed and Discount Received nominal accounts in the General Ledger—they are not cash/bank asset balances [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A business starts the year with $400 Provision for Doubtful Debts. Trade receivables at year-end are $14,000 and the business decides to maintain the provision at 2.5%. Calculate the adjustment to the Income Statement and state whether it is added as income or deducted as an expense. [4 marks]
questions.explanation:
Required closing provision = 2.5% × $14,000 = $350 [2 marks].
Decrease in provision = $400 - $350 = $50 reduction [1 mark].
Since the provision decreased, $50 is added to Gross Profit (credited as income) in the Income Statement [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Explain the accounting treatment of (a) Carriage Inwards, (b) Carriage Outwards, (c) Drawings in cash, and (d) Owner introducing a personal computer into the business. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Carriage Inwards: added to Purchases in Trading Account [1]. (b) Carriage Outwards: operating expense in Profit & Loss section [1]. (c) Drawings: reduces Capital in Balance Sheet (Dr Drawings, Cr Cash) [1]. (d) Personal computer: increases Non-Current Assets and Capital (Dr Office Equipment, Cr Capital) [1].

questions.questionText: Compare FIFO (First In, First Out) and AVCO (Weighted Average Cost) inventory valuation methods during a period of rising prices (inflation), stating the effect on Gross Profit and Closing Inventory value. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: During inflation, FIFO charges older cheaper stock to Cost of Sales, leaving newer higher-cost inventory on hand—resulting in higher Closing Inventory and higher reported Gross Profit [2 marks]. AVCO averages unit costs after each receipt, yielding intermediate Gross Profit and Closing Inventory values [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain why a business might show a healthy Net Profit of $20,000 on its Income Statement yet still suffer a bank overdraft (cash flow crisis). Give four specific reasons. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: 1. High credit sales not yet paid by customers. 2. Heavy cash spending on new non-current assets (equipment/vehicles). 3. Large owner cash drawings or loan repayments. 4. Cash tied up in excess unsold closing inventory [4 marks].

questions.questionText:
From the following balances as at 31 December 2025, prepare a Statement of Financial Position extract showing Net Assets and Capital section:
Premises $45,000; Equipment $15,000 (Acc Dep $3,000); Inventory $6,200; Trade Receivables $4,800; Bank $1,500; Trade Payables $3,500; 5-Year Bank Loan $10,000; Opening Capital $48,000; Net Profit $11,500; Drawings $3,500. [7 marks]
questions.explanation:
Non-Current Assets: Premises $45,000 + Equipment NBV $12,000 = $57,000 [2].
Current Assets: $6,200 + $4,800 + $1,500 = $12,500; Less Current Liabilities $3,500 = Working Capital $9,000 [2].
Less Non-Current Liability Loan $10,000 -> Net Assets = $57,000 + $9,000 - $10,000 = $56,000 [1].
Financed By Capital: $48,000 + $11,500 - $3,500 = $56,000 (balances!) [2].

questions.questionText:
Identify which accounting concept applies in each situation:
(a) Depreciation method should not be switched randomly from year to year.
(b) A $5 stapler is expensed immediately rather than depreciated over 5 years.
(c) Unpaid December telephone bill of $85 is included in 2025 expenses.
(d) Revenue is recognised when goods are delivered on credit, not when cash arrives later. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Consistency concept [1]. (b) Materiality concept [1]. (c) Accruals (Matching) concept [1]. (d) Realisation concept [1].
